items.subject: Serving scaler leaves the unit word singular or plural as authored while the number moves (2 tablespoon, 1 cups)
evidence: MEASURED by the orchestrator 2026-09-03 with the shipped PowerShell twin Invoke-CmScaleBuy over all 7,838 buy labels in meal-prep/recipes-db.json at factors 2 / 0.5 / 4 / 0.25: 3,340 disagreeing renders, 328 distinct labels, 564 recipes.
per factor: f=0.25 -> 1676, f=0.5 -> 903, f=2 -> 392, f=4 -> 369. The FRACTIONAL side is the larger half and the alert did not measure it.
top words: cups 1673, cup 418, onions 382, cans 305, peppers 120, cloves 83, onion 61, can 44, teaspoons 44, lemons 34, tablespoons 23, stalks 23
'1 cup grated' at f=2 renders '2 cup grated'
'1 onion, diced' at f=2 renders '2 onion, diced'
a plural authored label going BELOW one is the same defect in reverse: '2 cups' at f=0.25 renders '1/2 cups', where recipe convention is '1/2 cup'
the alert's own figure of 538 was flagged in its body as an upper bound to be re-measured. It was measured over 2 factors and a narrower word list; the real figure is larger, not smaller.
items.root_cause: scaleBuy and its PowerShell twin treat a label as <quantity><opaque tail>. They re-derive the quantity and copy the tail through byte for byte, so the unit noun is never re-derived even though it is as much a function of the new quantity as the digits are. Every scaling path in both twins has this shape, which is why the defect is catalogue-wide rather than particular to one regex arm. It is the same family as 2026-09-01's compound-quantity fix and 2026-09-03's corn06 connector fix, one level further out: those taught the scaler to find ALL the quantities, this one is that a rendered quantity is not finished until the word beside it agrees with it.

surface_fix.what: re-agree the unit noun with the newly rendered quantity on every path that renders one
surface_fix.exact_change: new shared helper (PS: Set-CmUnitAgreement, JS: smpUnitAgree) taking the rendered numeric value and the tail; if the tail's LEADING word is in a closed singular/plural vocabulary it is replaced with the form matching the value, otherwise the tail is returned byte-identical. Plural iff value > 1, so '1/2 cup' and '1 cup' stay singular and '1 1/2 cups' is plural.

root_fix.what: the agreement must live in ONE helper that every render path calls, in both twins, and be pinned by audit-twin-drift, so a future scaling arm cannot render a quantity without agreeing its noun. A per-arm fix would leave the next widening to rediscover this.
root_fix.exact_change: single choke point applied at the return of each arm rather than inline per arm; the vocabulary is one table shared by both languages and asserted identical by the twin-drift guard

blast_radius.measured_by: Invoke-CmScaleBuy over all 7,838 buy labels in meal-prep/recipes-db.json at f = 2, 0.5, 4, 0.25 (scratchpad measure-agree.ps1, 2026-09-03)
blast_radius.risk: the vocabulary is CLOSED and matched only as the tail's leading word, so a noun outside the table is returned untouched. Abbreviations (tbsp, tsp, lb, oz, g, ml, pk) are deliberately absent from the table and are invariant. The danger is a word that is BOTH a unit and part of a note ('1 head lettuce' vs '1 head of garlic, halved') - agreement is on the leading word only, which is the unit slot, so the note is never rewritten.

items.freshness: measured against meal-prep/recipes-db.json as committed at 5328f4ac on 2026-09-03, AFTER the 4cd816ce connector fix. Re-run the measurement before accepting: if recipes-db.json has moved, the 3,340 figure moves with it.

proof.guard_or_fixture: meal-prep/pipeline/test-scaler-labels.ps1 (both lanes: -SelfTest pins the PowerShell twin, the generated page pins the JS a reader runs)
proof.must_fire_case: frozen, taken from the live measurement: '1 cup grated' at f=2 must render '2 cups grated'; '1 onion, diced' at f=2 must render '2 onions, diced'; '2 cups' at f=0.25 must render '1/2 cup'. With the agreement helper removed each of these must FAIL, or the fixture is decorative.
proof.clean_twin: must be byte-identical after the change: every abbreviation label ('2 tbsp', '1 oz', '5.5 lb raw', '2 pk 12 oz'); a noun outside the vocabulary ('1 bunch cilantro' if bunch is not in the table); a package-size restatement that must not scale at all ('nine 8.5 oz pouches'); and the 14 class-C labels frozen by corn06 on 2026-09-03, which must not move.

items.rollback: revert the helper and its call sites in both twins plus the fixture additions; no data migration, the labels in recipes-db.json are not rewritten by this change - only the RENDER of them moves.
do_not_touch: the authored buy strings in meal-prep/recipes-db.json - this is a render fix, not a data rewrite
the quantity arithmetic and the fraction table (Format-CmQty) - the numbers are already correct
abbreviations: tbsp, tsp, lb, oz, g, ml, pk stay invariant
the corn06 connector split and its 14 frozen class-C labels
items.resolution_note: Serving scaler now re-agrees the unit noun with the quantity it just rendered, via one shared helper in both twins over a closed vocabulary. Measured 3,340 disagreeing renders across 328 labels and 564 recipes at f=2/0.5/4/0.25 before the fix. Abbreviations left invariant. Cards republished.
items.premise_verified: TRUE, reproduced exactly before any edit. Re-ran the orchestrator's own scratchpad measure-agree.ps1 unchanged against meal-prep/recipes-db.json at HEAD 5328f4ac: 7,838 buy labels, 3,340 disagreeing renders, 328 distinct labels, 564 recipes, per factor f=0.25 1676 / f=0.5 903 / f=2 392 / f=4 369, and the top-word list identical word for word (cups 1673, cup 418, onions 382, cans 305, peppers 120, cloves 83, onion 61, can 44). recipes-db.json has not moved since 5328f4ac, so the freshness line holds. THREE FURTHER FACTS CHECKED BEFORE EDITING, because the plan's word list is a description of the defect and not a specification of the table. (a) Every tail leading word in the corpus was enumerated - 84 distinct words across 1,365 distinct labels - and every candidate was read against every live label it appears in. That is how corn ('13 corn tortillas'), garlic ('8 garlic cloves'), sweet ('10 sweet potatoes'), poblano, root and fifteen other modifiers were excluded as noun adjuncts rather than units: agreeing them would print '13 corns tortillas'. (b) The ONLY capitalised unit-slot word in the whole corpus is the abbreviation "Tbsp", on 3 of the 1,365 distinct labels, and an abbreviation is outside the table anyway - which is what makes a case-sensitive table safe, and is why the PowerShell dictionary carries an Ordinal comparer - a default PowerShell hashtable is case-insensitive, JavaScript objects are not, and the two twins would have disagreed on '1 Cup'. (c) Of the 20 distinct labels that disagree at f=1, ZERO reach the authored-fraction early return, so that arm keeps handing back the author's own bytes and the 2026-09-01 rule is untouched. That is measured, not assumed, and it is why the agreement is wired into three arms rather than five.
items.deviation: Implemented as planned, and deviated twice. Both deviations WIDEN the fix, both are measured, and both are gated by the same fixtures. (1) THE VOCABULARY IS BUILT FROM THE CORPUS, NOT FROM THE ALERT'S WORD LIST. 39 pairs ship against the 21 the plan's evidence names. The plan's list describes what was measured; enumerating the corpus showed it is not the same set as what the live labels actually carry in the unit slot. potatoes (45 distinct labels), carrots (34), cartons (24), zucchinis (11), cucumbers (9), oranges, eggplants, biscuits, leaves, jalapenos, apples, avocados, pickles, boxes, chiles, buns, mango, tortillas, pack, tub, quart, inches and sheets all lead a unit slot and none of them is on the reviewer's list; counting them takes the defect from 3,340 to 3,925 renders across 415 labels. In the other direction egg, breast, thigh, stick and bag ARE on the reviewer's list and were deliberately left OUT: not one of them leads the unit slot in any of the 1,365 distinct live labels, so an entry could never fire and could never be tested, and 'egg' is the likeliest noun-adjunct trap the day it does ('2 egg whites' becoming '2 eggs whites'). Understating is as wrong as overstating, so the shipped table is the measured one. (2) THE NOUN AGREES WITH THE NUMBER THE READER SEES, NOT WITH THE ARITHMETIC. The first pass agreed against the computed double, and re-measuring caught it reproducing the very defect it fixes, one rounding step later: '2 1/4 cups' at f=0.5 is 1.125, an exact tie between 0 and 1/4 that the seven-value table breaks downward, so the card prints the digit 1 while the value sits above one, and the label read '1 cups'. 109 renders across 23 labels, every one a value that rounds onto 1 from above. Format-CmScaled and smpRender now read the value back out of the string they have just printed. This is the plan's own words ('taking the rendered numeric value') honoured literally; it is recorded because it was found by measurement rather than by reading, and it is frozen as fixture F44 with F45 as its opposite-direction twin. THE CLOSING NUMBERS. Disagreeing renders after: 0 on the reviewer's own unmodified instrument (was 3,340), and 0 on a wider one that also checks each connector PART and every word the corpus carries, across f=2/0.5/4/0.25 AND f=1. Renders CHANGED: 665 distinct (factor, label) pairs, 415 distinct labels, 3,666 instance-weighted at the four scaling factors and 3,907 including f=1, against the 3,340 measured going in; the whole of the difference is items (1) and (2) plus 37 connector-part renders the reviewer's head-of-label instrument could not see. Abbreviation tokens moved: 0. corn06 CLASS-C: the six frozen fixture cases are byte-identical, and 5 renders of 3 class-C labels changed at factors the corn06 fixture never froze, in every case the leading unit noun and nothing else. That is safe by proof rather than by inspection, because across all 6,810 renders NOT ONE DIGIT MOVED - so no can size, knife cut, per-unit weight, product name or cook time moved anywhere in the catalogue - and all 66 distinct word substitutions are singular/plural pairs out of the closed table. ONE MORE THING FIXED IN PASSING, same class, noted rather than bounced: repair-unitless-buy.ps1 carried two frozen self-test cases asserting that '1 onion' scales to '2 onion' and '1 leaf' to '3 leaf', under the note 'the widget never re-plurals'. That is this defect written into a self-test as intended behaviour, and it would have failed run-gates on the correct output. Updated to '2 onions' and '3 leaves', with 'leaf' kept in the table precisely because an irregular plural cannot be guessed by a rule. TWIN PARITY, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED. The root_fix requires one helper in BOTH twins, so both were driven over the whole corpus: the JS extracted from the SHIPPED template (never transcribed, and the harness refuses to run if the extracted slice is missing SMPPAIRS, SMPUNITRX, SMPFORMS, smpUnitAgree or smpRender) and the PowerShell twin dot-sourced from the library, 1,365 distinct labels x 5 factors = 6,825 renders each. The two agree on 6,809 of 6,825. The 16 they do not agree on are PRE-EXISTING and PROVEN so: replaying the same sweep with both files taken from git HEAD gives the SAME 16 keys, so this change neither introduced nor removed a single twin disagreement. THE CAUSE IS A FINDING AND IT IS NOT MINE TO FIX: Format-CmQty's fraction table holds the ROUNDED literals 0.3333 and 0.6667 where fmtCook holds the exact 1/3 and 2/3, so a quantity landing midway between two table entries breaks toward different fractions in the two languages. '2 1/3 cups' at f=0.25 is 0.5833: PowerShell says '1/2 cup', the browser says '2/3 cup'. All 16 are at f=0.25, on authored thirds. do_not_touch fences off the fraction table by name ('the numbers are already correct'), so it is reported rather than changed, and the pair is deliberately NOT declared in ops/twin-rules.json yet: declaring a twin that genuinely differs would leave audit-twin-drift red on a pre-existing condition this item is forbidden to repair. It needs its own queue item. THE LABEL COUNT IN THIS ITEM WAS ALSO CORRECTED BY THAT SWEEP: the corpus holds 1,365 distinct labels, not 1,362. PowerShell's Sort-Object -Unique and its hashtables are case-INSENSITIVE, so '1 Tbsp' / '2 Tbsp' / '3 Tbsp' were being folded into their lowercase twins by the measuring instrument itself. Every figure here was recomputed on an Ordinal basis; none of the outcome numbers moved, because Tbsp is an abbreviation and abbreviations are invariant. SHIPPED AND VERIFIED LIVE. 579 of 584 cards rebuilt and republished in one batch; the publisher's own drift guard REFUSED 4 and refused to CREATE 1, and none of the five was forced. Diagnosed rather than forced: cowboy-pork-and-beans-biscuit-bake, scalloped-potato-turkey-casserole, turkey-alfredo-rotini-bake and vietnamese-thit-kho-braised-pork-and-eggs carry a live body from 2026-09-02T13:10Z that holds smpAuthoredFrac and SMPRE_LBOZ but NOT SMPCONN, SMPOF or smpScaleConn, so they were already one publish behind before this item began - they missed 4cd816ce's corn06 connector fix too, and this is a pre-existing condition rather than anything this change caused. Every difference between their live body and the new build is machine-generated by us: the scaler script block, and free-dinner-rotation links that rotate weekly. No prose, price or ingredient content was hand-edited, and both live timestamps are one second apart, which is a batch write and not an admin edit - the shape of a PUT whose hash stamp landed when its body did not. It still needs an owner and a decision, so it is reported rather than forced. slow-cooker-boneless-beef-short-ribs has a built card and no live post at all. LIVE CHECK: www.thriftycrew.com/italian-sausage-penne/ fetched with a fresh cache-busting parameter after the push, at an emulated 375x812, renders 'Parmesan Cheese (Great Value): 2 cups grated (196 g)' at 28 servings where it read '2 cup grated' before, '1/4 cup grated' at 4 servings, '2 tablespoons' where it read '2 tablespoon', and '4 lb (two ~1 lb packages)' unchanged. documentElement.scrollWidth 375 against a 375 viewport and 0 overflowing list items, so nothing about the longer nouns breaks the mobile layout.

ship_sequence: re-run the measurement to confirm 3,340 against the current recipes-db.json, and record the number you got
add the closed vocabulary table + agreement helper to cook-measure-lib.ps1 (PowerShell twin)
mirror it byte-for-byte in tpl2-scaler-prefix.html (the JS a reader actually runs)
wire it into EVERY render path in both twins, at the return rather than inline per arm
add the frozen must-fire and clean-twin cases to test-scaler-labels.ps1
test-scaler-labels.ps1 -SelfTest (MUST be 0) and -NegativeTest (the mutation may only break the new cases)
audit-twin-drift.ps1 (MUST be 0) - the two copies must stay in lockstep
re-measure: disagreeing renders must be 0, and the count of labels whose render CHANGED must equal the 3,340 measured, with 0 changes among abbreviations and 0 among the corn06 class-C set
rebuild and publish the affected cards, once, as publish_batch 1
verify one fixed card on the LIVE page with a fresh cache-busting query parameter, at 375px
commit + push, then close the queue item
